# BISCAD

> A hosted build123d / OpenCascade CAD kernel behind a REST API and an MCP server. Send a build123d Python script, get back a real B-rep with stable face/edge ids (p0/f3, p0/e7), headless renders you can look at, analysis, build-step replay and exports (STEP, STL, GLB, 3MF, BREP, SVG, DXF). Units are millimetres.

Base URL: the origin serving this file (e.g. https://<host>). MCP endpoint: https://<host>/mcp (streamable HTTP).
Auth: `Authorization: Bearer bsc_...` (optional; without it you get a small anonymous per-IP quota). Get a key: `POST /v1/keys {"email": "..."}` → `{"api_key", "plan"}`.

## How to work (recommended loop)

1. Write a build123d script. End with `result = <shape or BuildPart.part>`, or call `show(a, b, ...)` for an assembly (one part per argument). Put tunable numbers in a top-level `params = {"width": 40, ...}` dict literal.
2. `POST /v1/build {"script", "params"?}` (MCP: `build_model`). Stateless. Read `ok`, `error`, `logs`, `summary` (volume, bbox, faces, edges per part).
3. Look at it: `GET /v1/versions/{vid}/render-grid.png` (MCP: `render_grid`) or `render.png?view=iso&highlight=p0/f3`. Do not claim a part is correct without looking.
4. Save: `POST /v1/documents {"name", "script", "params"?}` (MCP: `create_document`) → `version.id`. Iterate with `POST /v1/documents/{id}/versions {"script"?, "params"?, "parent"?, "message"?}` (MCP: `update_document`).
5. Before naming a face or edge, call `GET /v1/versions/{vid}/topology` (MCP: `get_topology`). Ids follow build123d order: `p0/f3` == `part.faces()[3]` of part 0. Each face also has a `persistent_id` like `p0/#1a2b3c4d`. It stays the same after parameter changes and added features. Use it in place of `p0/f3` to keep a reference across edits.
6. Check and ship: `POST /v1/versions/{vid}/check {"process": "fdm"|"cnc"|"sheet"}`, then `GET /v1/versions/{vid}/export/step`.
7. Explain to the human: link `GET /v1/versions/{vid}/report` (HTML design report), `/explainer.gif`, or summarise `GET /v1/versions/{vid}/steps`.

## Script rules

- No file/OS/network access (export_*, import_*, open, np.save/load are rejected; the server exports for you).
- Allowed imports: build123d, numpy, math, cmath, random, itertools, functools, operator, typing, dataclasses, enum, copy, collections, statistics, fractions, decimal, string, re, constraint_sketch.
- Not allowed: file or network access, open, exec, eval, compile, getattr/setattr/delattr, globals/locals/vars, dunder attributes or dunder strings, relative imports.
- print() output is returned in `logs`. Default time limit 60 s per job, with a memory cap.
- If neither `result` nor `show()` is used, the last build123d shape or BuildPart in scope is taken.

Minimal script:

    from build123d import *
    params = {"w": 60, "h": 30, "t": 6, "hole": 6.5}
    with BuildPart() as plate:
        Box(params["w"], params["h"], params["t"])
        with GridLocations(params["w"] - 15, params["h"] - 12, 2, 2):
            Hole(params["hole"] / 2)
        fillet(plate.edges().filter_by(Axis.Z), 3)
    result = plate.part

Constraint sketches (`from constraint_sketch import ConstraintSketch`): draw rough points, add constraints, solve.

    sketch = ConstraintSketch()
    a = sketch.point(0, 0, fixed=True); b = sketch.point(40, 3); c = sketch.point(38, 22); d = sketch.point(1, 20)
    bottom, right, top, left = sketch.line(a, b), sketch.line(b, c), sketch.line(c, d), sketch.line(d, a)
    sketch.horizontal(bottom); sketch.vertical(right); sketch.parallel(top, bottom); sketch.perpendicular(left, bottom)
    sketch.length(bottom, 60); sketch.distance(b, c, 25)
    hole = sketch.circle(sketch.point(30, 12), radius=4); sketch.radius(hole, 4)
    solution = sketch.solve()   # raises ConstraintSketchError naming the first conflicting constraint
    print(solution.degrees_of_freedom)   # 0 = fully constrained; position(point), radius(circle)
    result = extrude(solution.face(), 6)   # outer loop = lines in order, circles = holes

- Constraints: fixed, coincident, horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, length, distance (point-point), equal (lines or circles), angle (degrees, signed, first to second line), radius, tangent (line, circle), midpoint (point, line), point_on_line.
- Use `face(outer_loop_lines=[...], hole_circles=[...], plane=Plane.XZ)` when the sketch has construction lines.
- Example: GET /v1/examples, id `constrained_plate`.

## REST endpoints

- POST /v1/keys {email} → {api_key, plan}
- GET  /v1/me → {plan, usage:{calls_today, calls_month, compute_ms_month}, limits}
- POST /v1/build {script, params?, quality?: draft|normal|fine} → {ok, error?, logs, summary, scene, links:{scene, render, render_grid, report, explainer, step, stl, glb, viewer}}
- POST /v1/documents {name, script?, features?, params?, public?} → {document, version}
- GET  /v1/documents → {documents}; GET /v1/documents/{id} → {document, versions}
- POST /v1/documents/{id}/versions {script?, params?, features?, parent?, message?} → {version}
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid} → {id, document_id, parent, script, params, param_schema, status, error, logs, summary, created}
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/scene → scene JSON (format "biscad-scene" v1; base64 float32 positions/normals, uint32 indices; faces with start/count triangle ranges)
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/topology → face/edge descriptors (id, type, area, center, normal | radius, axis; edges: id, type, length)
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/steps → [{index, op, description, volume, faces, scene_url}]
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/render.png?view=iso|front|top|right|back|left|bottom&w=&h=&highlight=p0/f3,p0/e2
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/render-grid.png → 2x2 views
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/explainer.gif → captioned build animation
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/report → HTML design report
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/export/{fmt}, fmt ∈ step|stl|glb|3mf|brep|svg|dxf
- POST /v1/versions/{vid}/measure {a:"p0/f1", b:"p0/f7"} → {distance, angle_deg?, a, b}
- POST /v1/versions/{vid}/section {origin:[x,y,z], normal:[x,y,z]} → {area, svg}
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/mass?density=7.85 (g/cm³)
- POST /v1/versions/{vid}/check {process:"fdm"|"cnc"|"sheet"} → DFM report
- GET  /v1/diff?a={vid}&b={vid} → {volume_added, volume_removed, faces_added, faces_removed}
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/interference → {clashes:[{a,b,volume_mm3,center}], ok}
- GET  /v1/versions/{vid}/bom?density= → {items:[{item,name,quantity,ids,size_mm,volume_mm3}]}
- POST /v1/agent {prompt, script?, document_id?} → {ok, version, rounds} (text-to-CAD; needs a key and server-side ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
- POST /v1/import multipart `file` (step/stp/brep/stl) → {document, version}
- GET  /v1/examples → [{id, name, script}]  (quadruped, bracket, flange, gear, enclosure, leg)

A failed build is HTTP 200 with ok=false and an `error` message; fix the script and retry. HTTP 429 means quota exceeded.

Interactive API explorer (OpenAPI): /api/docs ; schema: /openapi.json

## MCP tools

build_model, create_document, update_document, list_documents, get_document, get_script, get_topology, render_view, render_grid, get_build_steps, measure, section, mass_properties, check_manufacturability, check_interference, bill_of_materials, diff_versions, export_model, list_examples, usage.

Setup:
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http biscad https://<host>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer bsc_..."`
- Claude Desktop / Cursor: {"mcpServers":{"biscad":{"url":"https://<host>/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer bsc_..."}}}}

## Limits and pricing

- Free: 2,000 builds/month, 10 text-to-CAD runs/month, all exports, MCP, no card.
- Pro: $12/month, 100,000 builds/month, 3-minute builds, priority workers.
- Scale: $0.0004 per build-second. Self-hosting is free (open source).

## Self-host

- `docker run -p 8000:8000 biscad` → http://localhost:8000 (site, /v1, /mcp)
- `./deploy/public.sh` → public https URL via a Cloudflare quick tunnel
